page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Aggregate fruits
lines: A bunch of fruitlets that develops from the
single flower is called an aggregate fruit
steps.why: The defining machinery is one FLOWER with FREE carpels - each free carpel becomes one fruitlet, so one flower yields a bunch.
common_mistakes: Writing syncarpous. Free (apocarpous) carpels are what give separate fruitlets.
Confusing aggregate (one flower) with composite (a whole inflorescence).
steps.memory_tip: One flower, free carpels, many fruitlets - an etaerio.
steps.margin_note: The words single flower and apocarpous both belong in the definition.

steps.label: Two examples
steps.why: Annona and lotus are the book's pair - both flowers have many free carpels, each ripening into a fruitlet on the same thalamus.
common_mistakes: Giving pineapple here. Pineapple is a composite fruit from a whole inflorescence.
steps.memory_tip: Custard apple - the bumps on its surface are the separate fruitlets.
